Coordinates, image matching, and quality control

coordinates-and-qc.Rmd

Coordinate errors can leave percent counts numerically unchanged while making the associated image evidence and ML crops wrong. Treat visual QC as a required handoff between import and interpretation.

library(pointcoral)

Two coordinate spaces

Imported .cpc rows can contain:

  • cpce_x, cpce_y: original CPCe display/region coordinates;
  • cpce_width, cpce_height: the coordinate-space dimensions used for conversion;
  • x_px, y_px: integer coordinates in the matched image; and
  • image_width, image_height: image dimensions in pixels.

convert_cpce_coords() uses proportional scaling independently for each axis.

example_points <- data.frame(
  cpce_x = c(0, 25, 50, 100),
  cpce_y = c(0, 10, 25, 50)
)

convert_cpce_coords(
  example_points,
  cpce_width = 100,
  cpce_height = 50,
  image_width = 1000,
  image_height = 500
)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 8
#>   cpce_x cpce_y cpce_width cpce_height image_width image_height  x_px  y_px
#>    <dbl>  <dbl>      <dbl>       <dbl>       <int>        <int> <int> <int>
#> 1      0      0        100          50        1000          500     0     0
#> 2     25     10        100          50        1000          500   250   100
#> 3     50     25        100          50        1000          500   500   250
#> 4    100     50        100          50        1000          500  1000   500

The function does not rotate, mirror, crop, georeference, or correct lens distortion. The current .cpc parser uses ROI maxima as the coordinate-space dimensions when available because that geometry fits the bundled fixtures. Other CPCe configurations require verification.

Basename image matching

match_images() searches under image_root and matches image_file by basename. This helps when a .cpc file contains an old Windows path but the same image now lives on macOS or Linux.

Basenames must be unique. If two directories contain transect_01.jpg, the first match is used with a warning. Rename files or separate projects before a release analysis; a successful basename match does not prove image identity.

Table validation 

example_dir <- system.file("extdata", package = "pointcoral")
points <- read_cpce_folder(example_dir, image_root = example_dir, recursive = FALSE)
validate_points(points)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   check severity     n details                      
#>   <chr> <chr>    <int> <chr>                        
#> 1 ok    info         0 No validation issues detected

To see the report structure, introduce deterministic problems in a copy:

bad <- points
bad$raw_label[1] <- NA_character_
bad$x_px[2] <- bad$image_width[2] + 50L
validate_points(bad)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   check                     severity     n details                              
#>   <chr>                     <chr>    <int> <chr>                                
#> 1 missing_raw_labels        warning      1 Rows with missing raw_label values   
#> 2 coordinates_outside_image warning      1 Pixel coordinates outside image boun…

Validation reports issues; it does not change the input or decide whether a row should be excluded.

Visual overlay 

write_qc_overlays(
  points,
  image_root = example_dir,
  out_dir = "project_outputs/qc",
  label_col = "raw_label"
)

Review at least:

  1. points near all four image edges;
  2. recognizable structures and the expected image orientation;
  3. labels around mixed or ambiguous benthic cover;
  4. out-of-frame, repeated, or unexpectedly clustered points; and
  5. the exact source image and CPCe file identity.

An overlay is evidence that points appear in plausible locations. It cannot confirm sampling randomness, taxonomic correctness, or ecological representativeness.

Units and conventions

Coordinates and patch/mask radii are in pixels, not centimetres or metres. Physical scale can differ among cameras, image crops, and survey protocols. Record the relationship between image pixels and field scale outside the package when physical-area interpretation matters.
